title: POC scoping - success criteria signoff (Acme Corp)
summary: AE + SE walked through proposed 4-week POC plan, defined measurable success criteria (latency, cost, quality thresholds), agreed on acceptance test format and reporting, and confirmed integration touches. Security asked for audit log retention and KMS notes. Next step: Redwood to send benchmark plan + test harness and schedule baseline run week of 2025-07-07.
next_steps: Avery: Send detailed benchmark plan + spreadsheet (includes sample queries) by 2025-07-01
Diego: Share test harness repo and CI instructions by 2025-07-02
Acme: Provide sample production prompt set (5k examples) by 2025-07-03
action_items: Avery Chen: Draft and send POC success-criteria doc with thresholds — due 2025-07-01
Diego Morales: Prepare runbook and k8s/VPC checklist for private deployment tests — due 2025-07-02
Liam O'Neill: Export sample dataset (5k prompts + expected tolkens) and upload to shared drive — due 2025-07-03
Sofia Ruiz: Confirm SSO/SAML and KMS requirements & share compliance contact — due 2025-07-04
transcript:
Header: 2025-06-25 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Acme CTO), Liam O'Neill (ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Security), Noah Kim (Platform)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda: align on success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan and acceptance tests so we can sign off and run the POC.
[00:22] Maya: Thanks, Avery. We're excited, main ask is predictable latencies and cost per 1k tokens. Also security stuff, ofc.
[00:35] Diego: Great, we'll propose a 4-week POC. Week 1 integration + baseline, week 2 tuning, week 3 optimizations + repeated runs, week 4 acceptance runs and final report. Does that line up with your timelines?
[00:50] Liam: Yes that's fine. We want a go/no-go by end of week 4. Important for us: p95 latency under 200 ms for typical prompt sizes (avg ~120 tokens), error rate < 0.5%, and quality regression < 2% vs current model baseline on the eval set.
[01:15] Priya: To confirm, when you say "quality regression" do you mean automated metric or human eval?
[01:22] Liam: Automated primary (BLEU/ROUGE style + a in-domain scoring script) and a 5% sample for human spot-checks. Pass threshold is no more than 2% drop in the automated metric and no systemic failures in the human sample.
[01:40] Maya: Also want cost guidance — target average cost per 1k tokens < $1.20 for production-ish load, and we'd like Redwood's recommendations on batching/quantization to hit that.
[01:55] Diego: We'll include cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs private in the plan. For the POC acceptance run we'll measure token-level cost using your sample traffic and Redwood's telemetry.
[02:10] Noah: For sizing: our expected peak concurrency is ~120 concurrent reqs, avg tokens per request 120 outbound + 40 inbound, throughput target 350 rps sustained during spikes.
[02:28] Priya: Ok noted — we'll size the benchmark to simulate that pattern (arrival rate, token distro). For the acceptance run we recommend 3 x 10 minute windows: steady, spike, and long-tail tests.
[02:45] Maya: What about tail latency? We care about p99 as well — want p99 < 350 ms.
[02:52] Diego: We'll report p50/p95/p99 and 95th-token latency too. Also include percent of requests served from KV/prefix cache during runs since that impacts cost.
[03:10] Sofia: Security: we need SOC2 attestations, audit log retention of 13 months, SSO/SAML support and KMS with customer-managed keys. Also confirm Redwood doesn't retain unencrypted customer payloads.
[03:33] Avery: We will attach our SOC2 cert and security pack. For KMS we support customer KMS in Private; for hosted might be partnership options — we'll clarify in the security deck.
[03:48] Sofia: Also need detailed audit log schema and retention policy to evaluate with our compliance team.
[03:55] Jordan: We'll include an audit log sample and retention options in the security appendix.
[04:10] Liam: On reporting format, we'd like a CSV summary plus an HTML dashboard: per-test row with test id, window type, avg latency, p95, p99, error rate, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and quality score. Also a pass/fail column computed against thresholds.
[04:30] Priya: Perfect — Redwood will provide both a CSV export and a link to the Redwood Console run dashboard. We'll also include the raw traces for any failed tests.
[04:45] Maya: For acceptance criteria summary — can you read back the go/no-go thresholds so we have them captured?
[04:52] Diego: Sure. Go if: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 350 ms, error rate <= 0.5%, automated quality metric drop <= 2% vs baseline, cost per 1k tokens <= $1.20 (or agreed host/dedicated price), and no critical security blockers (SOC2 ok, KMS/SSO mechanism agreed). Otherwise no-go.
[05:20] Maya: That looks right. On reporting cadence we want a weekly status during the POC with the final acceptance report on the last day.
[05:30] Avery: We'll send a benchmark plan spreadsheet with sample queries, traffic shapes and the evaluation script. Diego will share the runbook.
[05:40] Liam: A couple of questions about model variants — can you automatically fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if latency spikes?
[05:52] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports model variants and routing policies. For the POC we'll test a default model and a quantized variant. We can show cost/quality delta in the acceptance report. Note: some proper names may show up weird in the transcript, we might mis-say Redwood product names as Red wood or Redwood infer — small transcription glitches.
[06:15] Priya: For the benchmark itself we recommend three buckets of prompts: small (<=64 tokens), medium (~120 tokens), large (>=300 tokens) and weight them based on your traffic distribution. We'll include those weights in the spreadsheet.
[06:32] Noah: Any infra constraints for the private tests? We run in GCP with VPC peering and private IPs, and need a plan for egress and VPC endpoints.
[06:42] Diego: We'll include a k8s/VPC checklist. For private deployment we can do a direct peering or a private gateway. We'll also list required firewall rules.
[06:55] Sofia: On data retention: for baseline runs we prefer Redwood not store raw payloads beyond 14 days unless encrypted and requested for debugging.
[07:05] Avery: Noted, we'll propose 14-day retention for debug payloads and show options for longer retention if you need it.
[07:18] Maya: Back to acceptance tests: how long should the acceptance run be? We want it long enough to validate tail and cost — maybe a 4-hour run?
[07:28] Diego: We typically do a combined acceptance window: three stress windows (10m spike x3) plus an extended soak of 60-90 minutes for cost and stability. If you prefer a full 4-hour long-run we can do that as well; it just increases cloud usage.
[07:45] Liam: Let's do the extended soak 90 minutes plus the three 10-minute windows. That should surface tail behaviors without a full 4-hour blowout.
[07:55] Priya: We'll capture sample traces for requests that hit p99 and attach the failing prompts.
[08:03] Maya: How will we measure quality for long prompts? Our baseline includes some multi-turn context tests.
[08:12] Diego: We'll run both stateless and multi-turn scenarios. For multi-turn we'll measure final-turn relevancy and also track token growth and KV cache hit rate.
[08:25] Liam: Ok rough timeline confirms: Send docs by 7/1, repo by 7/2, sample prompts by 7/3, baseline run week of 7/7, tuning week 7/14, optimizations 7/21, acceptance run week 7/28 with report by 7/30.
[08:45] Avery: I'll capture that. Anything else?
[08:49] Sofia: Please include an SLA-like statement for the POC run availability expectations so our ops team can plan.
[08:58] Jordan: We'll include expected uptime and a contact for on-call during the runs.
[09:05] Maya: Great. On pricing if the POC looks good, we'll evaluate dedicated capacity quotes. Can you send a ballpark?
[09:12] Avery: We'll include ballpark host vs dedicated TCO in the spreadsheet; final pricing post-POC.
[09:20] Maya: Ok thanks everyone, let's reconvene after the baseline.
[09:25] (cross talk)
[51:30] Avery: Quick recap: action items and owners, benchmark plan deliverable dates (7/1-7/3), baseline run week of 7/7, acceptance run week of 7/28. We'll track weekly status. Any blocking items?
[51:48] Maya: No blockers from our side, thanks.
[51:52] Diego: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.

End of call.
